title: Around the World in Eighty Days

image.note: Title over a world map with a dotted route circling the globe; a steamship, a train and an elephant along the way

pages.text:
1. The Impossible Wager
2. Off at Once
3. A Rescue in India
4. Chased Across the World
5. Trouble at Every Turn
6. The Race Against Time
7. One Day Saved

Around the World in Eighty Days was written by Jules Verne and first published in 1873. Jules Verne was fascinated by the new machines of his age, the steamships and railways that were suddenly making the world feel smaller. This thrilling race around the globe captures the excitement of travel and adventure, and remains one of the most beloved journeys in all of fiction.

Mr Phileas Fogg was the most precise and punctual gentleman in all of London. He did everything exactly by the clock and was never a second late for anything. One evening, at his club, the gentlemen were discussing a bold claim in the newspaper: that thanks to new railways and steamships, a person could now travel all the way around the whole world in just eighty days.

image.note: A calm, precise Victorian gentleman at a gentlemen's club, a newspaper open; other members debating; a bold claim

pages.text: The other gentlemen scoffed that it could never be done. But cool Mr Fogg calmly declared that it could, and wagered his entire fortune that he would do it himself, and return to that very room in exactly eighty days. The astonished gentlemen took the bet at once. And so, with no fuss whatsoever, Mr Fogg resolved to circle the globe against the clock.

image.note: Mr Fogg calmly shaking hands on an enormous wager; astonished club members; a great adventure begun with no fuss

pages.text: Mr Fogg had just hired a lively new French servant named Passepartout, who had hoped for a quiet, restful position. Instead, within hours, he found himself packing a single bag and dashing off to circle the entire planet. The two set off that very night, catching the first train, with eighty days to cross the whole world and not one to spare.

image.note: Mr Fogg and his flustered servant Passepartout dashing to catch a train with one small bag; the race is on; comic energy

pages.text: But there was a complication. A robbery had just taken place in London, and a stubborn detective named Fix wrongly became convinced that the mysterious, sudden traveller Mr Fogg was the thief, fleeing the country. So Fix set off after them, determined to arrest Fogg. All around the world, unknown to Fogg, the detective would follow, scheming to delay and catch him.

image.note: A suspicious detective, Fix, spotting Fogg boarding a ship; secretly following; a mistaken pursuit begins

pages.text: Their journey took them by steamship and railway across seas and continents. In India, the railway line was unfinished, so, undaunted, Mr Fogg simply bought an elephant to carry them onward through the jungle. It was there that they came upon a young woman, Aouda, in grave danger, about to be forced into a terrible fate against her will.

image.note: Mr Fogg, Passepartout and a guide riding an elephant through an Indian jungle; a young woman in peril ahead

pages.text: Though every hour was precious to his wager, Mr Fogg did not hesitate. He and Passepartout bravely and cleverly rescued the young woman, Aouda, and brought her safely away with them. From then on she travelled at their side. Beneath his cold, punctual manner, it turned out, Mr Fogg had a truly good and generous heart, and would risk even his fortune to do what was right.

image.note: Fogg and Passepartout cleverly rescuing Aouda and helping her to safety; courage and kindness; the cold man's warm heart

pages.text: On they raced, across Asia and over the sea to Hong Kong and beyond. All the while, the detective Fix schemed to slow them down, hoping to delay Fogg until an arrest warrant could reach him. At one point Fix even tricked poor Passepartout, causing the loyal servant to be separated from his master and lost in a strange foreign city. But nothing could shake Mr Fogg's calm determination.

image.note: A busy Asian port; the sneaky detective Fix plotting; Passepartout separated and lost in a crowd; obstacles mounting

pages.text: Time and again, trouble threw itself in their path: missed boats, wild weather, and the detective's meddling. Yet with cool cleverness and a great deal of money spent freely, Mr Fogg overcame every setback. He hired special trains, chartered whole ships, and never once panicked, keeping always to his precise reckoning of the days. The world was wide, but Fogg was unstoppable.

image.note: Fogg chartering a ship in a storm, spending freely, utterly calm; overcoming obstacle after obstacle; determined

pages.text: Crossing the great American West by train, they met fresh dangers, a broken bridge, and even an attack on the railway that carried Passepartout off. Once more Mr Fogg, losing precious time, refused to abandon his friend and bravely rescued him before continuing. Every rescue cost him hours he could not spare, but Fogg would not leave a companion behind for any wager in the world.

image.note: A train crossing the vast American plains in danger; Fogg bravely rescuing Passepartout; loyalty above winning

pages.text: At last they reached the eastern coast of America and caught a ship for England, with the days running dangerously short. When even that ship threatened to be too slow, the resourceful Mr Fogg took charge of the vessel itself to drive it onward at full speed. The great circle of the world was nearly closed. Only the final dash across the sea to England remained.

image.note: A steamship racing at full speed across the Atlantic toward England; Fogg urging it on; the finish in sight; thrilling

pages.text: They reached England at last, and raced for London. But there, disaster struck. The detective Fix, still believing Fogg a thief, finally arrested him, and held him locked up for several precious hours before the mistake was discovered and Fogg was freed. By the time the innocent Mr Fogg reached London, it seemed he was too late. The eighty days, he believed, had run out. He had lost everything.

image.note: Fogg wrongly arrested and delayed; released too late; arriving in London believing all is lost; crushing disappointment

pages.text: Mr Fogg accepted his ruin with quiet dignity, having lost his whole fortune, or so he thought. His one comfort was Aouda, who had come to love him, and he her, and the two agreed to marry. Passepartout was sent to arrange the wedding for the very next day. And it was there, entirely by accident, that the most wonderful mistake was discovered.

image.note: Fogg and Aouda quietly agreeing to marry despite his ruin; tender; a happy love amid apparent defeat

pages.text: Passepartout burst back in with astonishing news. In travelling eastward around the whole world, always towards the rising sun, they had gained a full extra day without ever noticing it. It was not the day they thought at all. Mr Fogg had, in truth, arrived with time to spare. He was not too late. He had won his impossible wager after all.

image.note: Passepartout bursting in with joyful news; Fogg realising he has gained a day travelling east; astonished delight

pages.text: Mr Fogg rushed to his club and strode in at the precise final second, to the amazement of all the gentlemen, and won his enormous wager. But he had gained something far greater than money on his journey round the world. He had found true friends in Passepartout and a loving wife in Aouda. The precise, lonely gentleman had circled the globe, and come home with a heart full of warmth.

image.note: Fogg striding into his club at the last second, winning the bet; but truly rich in friends and love; joyful, closing
